conviction_note: A small, mostly mechanical positive: Q2 (Jun-Aug) laps a weak quarter (OP 925m, -25% yoy) and now includes Care'x (ケアレックス), which added about 2.1億 of OP in Q1. Against that, Q1's underlying OP excluding the 優待 swing and Care'x was down about 15%, and nothing big is likely to be added: no H1 forecast exists, the company revises in January rather than at H1, and the 50-yen interim dividend is already public. The findings sum to +0.25. The scaled number is (2*0.56-1)*1.8 = +0.22. Both measurements are small and agree in sign.
bar: Company FY2027/2 plan: OP 5,800m, ordinary 5,950m, NP 3,600m, no H1 guidance (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708589896.pdf). No IFIS consensus and no analyst coverage (https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportTop?bcode=8125). The working bar is H1 OP as a share of the full-year plan against the company's own record: 49.6% (FY24/2), 43.7% (FY25/2), 48.3% (FY26/2), from https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=8125. My H1 OP estimate of about 28億 is 48% of 58億, so it sits inside that range. The bar is the company's own plan and not a market estimate, so every size is capped small.
positioning_check: JPX short register 0.0% (no disclosed position at or above 0.5%, as of 2026-09-29; https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html), unchanged. 信用倍率 0.81 per the baseline and kabutan (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=8125), so margin shorts exceed margin longs. No options, no skew. The stock is down 7.6% over 20 sessions and 5.5% over 5, and -2.3% this morning at 1,818 on no company disclosure: it slid from 1,973 on 09-25 to 1,819 on 10-08, the latest filing being an immaterial subsidiary merger on 09-24. priced_lean_pct is +0.43. The retail register is heavy: 37,385 holders, 5.5% dividend yield plus a 10,000-yen hotel voucher.

findings.finding: Q2 FY27 (Jun-Aug 2026) is compared with a weak Q2 FY26 (OP 925m, ordinary 994m, -22% yoy) that did not include Care'x, which was acquired in Sept 2025. In Q1 FY27 the 介護レンタル segment's OP rose from 1.2億 to 3.3億 (+2.1億) on Care'x consolidation, so Q2 should carry a similar mechanical uplift and H1 should print as up year on year on kabutan's headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (headline OP +10.9%) rose 1.79% the next session (2026-07-10, kabutan 'ワキタが反発、第１四半期２ケタ営業増益'). H1 FY26, with a headline ordinary profit down 8% and Q2 down 22%, fell 2.52% (2025-10-10 to 10-14, Yahoo daily bars).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, because the Q1 deck is public. But the stock has fallen 7.8% since 09-25 with no company news, and margin shorts exceed longs (0.81). If holders were positioned for an H1 yoy-growth headline, the stock would not be sliding into the print. No analyst publishes a Q2 number, so nobody has stated the low-comp arithmetic.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 comp from https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=8125 (25.06-08 OP 925m) and H1 FY26 deck https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251010/140120251009570970.pdf; the Care'x uplift rests on the same Q1 deck as finding 2 (that deck counts once).

findings.finding: Q1 FY27's +10.9% OP headline rests on a 2.4億 swing in 株主優待 costs (a 1.5億 provision in Q1 FY26 against a 0.8億 reversal in Q1 FY27). Excluding that swing and Care'x's roughly 2.1億, underlying OP fell about 15%: the construction-machinery segment -15.2% (8.8億 vs 10.3億), group rental subsidiaries -29.7% and 'other construction machinery' subsidiaries -33.2%, on weak machine sales and IT and hiring spend. If Q2 repeats this, the quality of the H1 growth is poor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26/2 results with OP -17% and the January cut: -4.84% on 2026-04-09 to 04-10. The January 2026 downward revision, blamed on upfront investment not earning its return, fell ('ワキタが反落', 2026-01-26).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because the segment table is public and the stock has already slid. It is still filed, because a second quarter of falling construction-segment profit would be new, and Q2 is the seasonally weakest quarter, where cost growth shows most.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1. The Q1 tanshin text at https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708589896.pdf confirms the 0.8億 reversal and weak machine sales.

findings.finding: Two counterparty and industry reads on Jun-Aug rental and equipment demand lean firm. Kanamoto's May-Jul 2026 ordinary profit rose 44% yoy, with rental demand firm on public works plus logistics and data-centre construction. Japan's domestic construction-machine shipments rose 4.0% yoy in July (a second straight increase), though domestic Apr-Jul was only +1.0% and hydraulic excavators were -5.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Wakita's own rental line rose in Q1 while machine sales fell.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy. Kanamoto is Hokkaido- and Tohoku-heavy while Wakita is Kansai-based, and peer reads are rarely carried across to an uncovered name like this one. If they had been, the stock would not be making new lows into the print.
findings.independence: https://newswitch.jp/p/50185 (日刊工業新聞, 2026-09-01: 建機工 July shipments, domestic +4.0%)

findings.finding: The Kansai post-Expo hangover sits against Wakita's Q2. Its Osaka hotel's unit price fell after the Expo closed (stated in Q1), and Q2 FY26 (Jun-Aug 2025) was peak Expo season. Kansai peer Nishio HD's Apr-Jun 2026 ordinary profit fell 20% on the Expo-demand reversal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for Wakita. Nishio fell sharply on its Expo-reversal prints (kabutan 2026-02-05 and 2026-05-12).
findings.why_not_priced: Small and partly priced. The real-estate segment is about 6% of sales, and Q1 real-estate profit still rose 7.8% despite the hotel. Nobody has carried the peak-Expo Q2 comp across to this name.
findings.independence: Wakita's own Q1 tanshin segment text (hotel unit price fall after the Expo closed): https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708589896.pdf

findings.finding: Management states a 2028/2 ROE target of 5.0% (actual 3.4%), lists 資本構成の検討 among capital-efficiency measures, and has committed to 100 yen or more a year through FY28/2 (payout above 130%). That leaves room for a capital-return add-on at H1, but there is no document saying one is coming, and the 50-yen interim is already announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raising the dividend to 100 yen at the FY25/2 results: +5.58% (2025-04-11 to 04-14). The interim-dividend introduction: up against a weak market (kabutan 2026-06-26).
findings.why_not_priced: A buyback is not expected: the company has bought back almost nothing (65m in FY25), and cash fell 57億 in Q1. The probability is low, so the point size is tiny, but the upside tail is real for a retail-heavy register.
findings.independence: Interim-dividend notice https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260625/140120260625579376.pdf (the 50 yen is to be formally resolved at the October board).

outside_window.finding: Wakita's habit is to revise its full-year forecast in late January (24/01/26 and 26/01/23), not at H1. Any FY27 plan risk from the weak construction segment would most likely surface around January 2027.
The absorption merger of the hotel-land subsidiary コルディア becomes effective 2027-01-01. It is immaterial (net assets 105m).

baseline_tension: Mild agreement with the priced lean (+0.43, from the negative run-up and a margin ratio below 1) and mild disagreement with the falling tape. The strongest positive the release could carry is an unsignalled buyback or a capital-structure step; I looked for it and found only the ROE-target language. The strongest negative would be a 優待 cut or an early forecast trim, and I found no sign of either.
lessons_applied: nothing changed: rule 1 (public-series negatives move p_up toward 50) leaves p_up at 56, because the draft already leaned only mildly positive and its one public-data negative (-0.3) was sized as partly priced; rule 2 (look for the strongest positive) was already done (buyback/capital-structure check, filed at +0.1)
